topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the lecture series, and presents the session's key learning objectives.

topics.label: Intrinsic mutational processes versus environmental drivers of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and explore the debate over whether malignancies are primarily driven by intrinsic random mutations or environmental exposures.

topics.label: Pathogen-driven carcinogenesis and Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens drive oncogenesis, focusing on Burkitt lymphoma as a model of infection-associated malignant transformation.

topics.label: Biochemical mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biochemical mechanisms through which physical radiation and metabolically activated chemical carcinogens induce DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, microenvironment, and host tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic promotional processes, microenvironmental inflammation, and cellular proliferative states cooperate with mutations to facilitate tumor development.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogen exposure and proving carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the experimental, genomic, and epidemiological methodologies used to identify carcinogen exposures and evaluate whether specific agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Closing remarks on cancer risk and exposure balance
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic reviews the main takeaways on environmental carcinogenesis and reflects on how individuals weigh the risks and benefits of various exposures.
